text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.6% today, continuing a steep two-week decline of 7.3%. The drop reflects broader uncertainty around oil prices: U.S. crude is trading at $96.41 per barrel, down sharply this week after initial optimism around Iran-U.S. talks at the U.N. faded when Trump rejected Iran's ceasefire proposal and signaled renewed military action. Lower oil prices directly cut into the earnings potential of oil producers like ConocoPhillips.

The geopolitical situation creates conflicting pressures. While Trump's hardline stance could tighten global oil supplies and support prices, the market is currently pricing in near-term caution—oil fell nearly 8% last week as peace-talk hopes briefly lifted. Saudi Arabia's rising exports despite infrastructure attacks are also keeping supply more abundant than feared, which weighs on the price outlook that matters most to ConocoPhillips' bottom line.
